Hub C and bridge E are both an average of 1.5 hops from the rest and tie at 0.67, followed by D 0.60, B and F 0.50, A 0.46, and the pendant node G at 0.35." width="100%"} Closeness centrality is the reciprocal of a node's average shortest-path distance to the nodes it can reach. A node that is only a hop or two from everyone else scores close to `1`, while a node on the periphery, many hops from most of the graph, scores low. The formula is `C(v) = r / Σ d(v,u)`, summed over the `r` nodes `u` reachable from `v`. In a disconnected graph that ratio alone would over-reward nodes in small components (two nodes joined by one edge would both score `1`), so by default the score is also multiplied by `r / (n - 1)`, the fraction of the graph that `v` can reach. This is the Wasserman-Faust correction; set `wf_improved=False` to turn it off. On a connected graph `r = n - 1` and the correction has no effect. Nodes that reach nothing score `0`. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) distances are total edge weights (Dijkstra's algorithm), so closeness is consistent with `shortest_path_length()`; on an unweighted graph they are hop counts. For a reachability-based measure that sums `1 / d` instead of averaging `d`, see `harmonic_centrality()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Direction for measuring distances in directed graphs where: (1) `"out"` follows edges in their direction, measuring how close `v` is *to* others (default), (2) `"in"` follows edges in reverse, measuring how close others are *to* `v`, and (3) `"all"` ignores edge directions. Ignored for undirected graphs. Note that NetworkX's `closeness_centrality()` uses incoming distances, which corresponds to `mode="in"`. [wf_improved]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (the default), scale each score by the fraction of other nodes it can reach (the Wasserman-Faust correction). If `False`, use only the reachable nodes. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distances by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph: weights are used on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) and hop counts otherwise, the same rule `shortest_path()` uses. Pass `True` or `False` to override. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`; weights must be non-negative. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store closeness scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `"closeness_centrality"`. Overwrites the column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to closeness scores (range `[0, 1]`). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path, the middle node is the fewest hops from everyone else, so it has the highest closeness while the two ends have the lowest: ::: {#5798bf3a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) scores = graph.closeness_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(c, 3) for nid, c in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0.4, 'B': 0.571, 'C': 0.667, 'D': 0.571, 'E': 0.4} ``` ::: ::: In a disconnected graph the Wasserman-Faust correction keeps the two nodes of a lone edge from outranking the hub of a larger star. Turning it off shows the difference: ::: {#9d86cbb2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Hub", "A", "B", "C", "X", "Y"]) .add_edges([("Hub", "A"), ("Hub", "B"), ("Hub", "C"), ("X", "Y")]) ) corrected = graph.closeness_centrality(return_dict=True) raw = graph.closeness_centrality(wf_improved=False, return_dict=True) { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): (round(corrected[nid], 2), round(raw[nid], 2)) for nid in sorted(corrected) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'Hub': (0.6, 1.0), 'A': (0.36, 0.6), 'B': (0.36, 0.6), 'C': (0.36, 0.6), 'X': (0.2, 1.0), 'Y': (0.2, 1.0)} ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph, `mode=` decides whether distances are measured from or to each node. In a chain, the source reaches everyone but nothing reaches it: ::: {#688a0107 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) out_scores = graph.closeness_centrality(mode="out", return_dict=True) in_scores = graph.closeness_centrality(mode="in", return_dict=True) { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): (round(out_scores[nid], 2), round(in_scores[nid], 2)) for nid in sorted(out_scores) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'A': (0.67, 0.0), 'B': (0.5, 0.5), 'C': (0.0, 0.67)} ``` ::: ::: Without `return_dict=`, the scores are stored as a node attribute for later use: ::: {#81032860 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("B", "D")]) .closeness_centrality(attr_name="closeness") ) graph.get_node_df().select(["label", "closeness"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
